Subject: Exploring Redwood for K-12 analytics (FERPA / limited BAA questions)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Greenfield USD is evaluating a small pilot to surface classroom-level insights and anonymized engagement metrics across ~12 schools. A few items legal asks we confirm up front so we can thread this into procurement: 

- Can Redwood sign a FERPA addendum for student education records?
- For a subset of records (student health/mental-health notes) our counsel requires a limited BAA scope — is that something you can support on a per-dataset basis?
- We need a subprocessor list and a view on any potential cross-border transfers (state residency requirement: data must remain in CA).
- Timeline: pilot start targeted March 15; we need contract language and security evidence (SOC 2) by March 1 to be on track.

I've attached our RFP summary for context. Small ask: could you send a short note back outlining feasibility and who from Redwood legal/security we should loop?

Best,
Tanya Santos

Greenfield Unified School District

Hi Tanya — thanks for the clear summary and the RFP. High-level answers and next steps below. I copied Monica (sales engineering) and Karthik (privacy/compliance) to coordinate the technical and contract follow-ups.

Quick feasibility summary:
- FERPA: Yes — Redwood can sign a FERPA addendum. We treat student education records as customer data and can commit to the FERPA controls in an addendum.
- Limited BAA scope: We can support a scoped BAA that covers ingestion and storage of a clearly defined dataset (e.g., health/mental-health notes). The typical pattern is: customer-designated dataset + field-level access controls + audit logging.
- Subprocessors & residency: I've attached a draft subprocessor list and our standard DPA template. We operate in multiple cloud regions; for a CA residency requirement we can offer Dedicated capacity or Private (VPC) deployment options to keep data within the US-west (CA) region. Some subprocessors (managed network/monitoring) may be US-based third parties — see draft list.
- Evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II and our security questionnaire answers. For HIPAA/BAA evidence we can provide our security controls mapping and audit artifacts during procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica to outline the technical deployment options and confirm which subprocessors are involved for a CA-only residency.
2) Karthik/legal to review the RFP and call out contract redlines we cannot accept vs items we can accommodate.
3) Quick working session next week (30m) to align on pilot scope and deliverables (dates).

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_template_v1.docx, subprocessor_list_draft.csv

I can make time Friday morning or early next week — what works?

Thanks,

Hi Tanya — following up with the technical notes for the pilot. I pulled together the likely deployment patterns and suggested mitigations to meet the CA residency + limited BAA constraints. Summary below; attaching a simple network diagram and the current draft subprocessor CSV.

Data flow (recommended):
- Ingest: Student records uploaded from your SIS via secure SFTP or direct API into a customer-dedicated S3 bucket in us-west-1 (CA region).
- Processing: Model inference happens on Dedicated capacity deployed in the same region; KV caches and logs can be optionally disabled for the pilot to minimize persisted data.
- Output: Analytics artifacts (aggregated metrics) are exported to a separate bucket with fine-grained IAM and lifecycle policies.

Controls we recommend enabling for this pilot:
- Private (VPC) deployment with region pinned to us-west-1
- Field-level pseudonymization of identifiers prior to model input (we can provide a tokenization library or you can preprocess)
- Retention policy: default 30 days for raw inputs; aggregated outputs retained as needed (we can accept contract-level retention constraints)
- Subprocessor constraints: Redwood can limit nonessential subprocessors for the pilot and provide 30-day notification for any changes.

Known subprocessors in the draft list: cloud object storage provider (us-based), metrics provider (US), security monitoring vendor (US). None are located outside the US in the current draft but please review the CSV for details.

Proposed pilot checklist (short):
- Contract: FERPA addendum + scoped BAA redline review by next Tue (23rd)
- Security: SOC 2 Type II report + security questionnaire by next Fri (27th)
- Deployment: provision Dedicated pilot environment in us-west-1 (estim. 5 business days)
- Ops: confirm onboarding contact and test dataset (PII removed/pseudonymized)

Attachments: subprocessor_list_draft.csv, network_diagram.png
Drive link with expanded notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleDoc

Subject: RE: Exploring Redwood for K-12 analytics (FERPA / limited BAA questions)

Jonas / Monica — thanks for the quick replies and the materials. I represent Greenfield for the contracting piece and I took a look at the DPA template and subprocessor list. A few contract items we need to flag before procurement will sign: 

1) Subprocessor notification and consent: we need explicit 30-day notice for new subprocessors and ability to object to a specific subprocessor that will handle student education records.
2) Data residency: contract must prohibit cross-border transfers of covered student data (data must remain within California). Please confirm whether Redwood will accept a CA-only residency guarantee for the pilot under Dedicated capacity or Private deployment.
3) Deletion SLA: for covered records, we need a contractual deletion guarantee of 30 days post-request, with audit logs confirming deletion.
4) Scoped BAA: if Redwood will agree to a limited BAA for student health notes, we need a clear definition of the dataset and an annex describing permitted uses and personnel access.
5) Audit evidence: please provide SOC 2 Type II report and any HIPAA controls mapping you have; we may request redacted reports under NDA.

A couple of clarifying technical questions (copied from Monica's note):
- Can you confirm whether any subprocessors perform analytics processing themselves (vs Redwood-only processing)?
- If pseudonymization is provided by Redwood, will the pseudonymization keys be customer-managed?

I've attached a short file with proposed redlines to the DPA for our counsel to start with (proposed_redlines.docx).

Would be helpful to have a short call on Wednesday morning (2/18) to align on where we can accept language vs where Greenfield needs firm commitments. If you can confirm the SOC 2 delivery path (NDA required?) and the CA-residency feasibility that will speed things up.

Thanks,
Ravi Shah
Counsel — EdTech Partners (on behalf of Greenfield USD)
